print((out/'manuscript.txt').read_text()[:38000])

strengths: The task and dataset provide the main basis for weak acceptance. Identifying, segmenting, and tracking individual sounding objects addresses a meaningful gap between audio-visual semantic segmentation and conventional video instance segmentation. Figure 1 clearly illustrates why distinguishing same-category instances and their sounding intervals matters.

AVISeg represents a substantial annotation contribution: 94,074 masks across 56,871 frames from 926 videos, covering 26 categories with an average duration of 61.4 seconds. The inclusion of silent frames and multiple simultaneous sources makes the benchmark useful for studying audio-dependent object selection and temporal association. SAM-assisted annotation followed by repeated manual refinement is a sensible construction process.

The baseline has convincing comparative support within this benchmark. Under the reported common ResNet-50 backbone and training schedule, Table 2 reports 42.78 FSLA, 61.73 HOTA, and 40.57 mAP, exceeding the strongest competing result for each metric by 3.29, 4.25, and 2.73 points, respectively. Improvements on established HOTA and mAP metrics provide evidence independent of the proposed FSLA metric.

The ablations support the usefulness of audio fusion at both levels. Adding video-level fusion to frame-level fusion raises HOTA from 59.59 to 61.73 and mAP from 39.06 to 40.57. The architecture is understandable, its relationship to Mask2Former and VITA is acknowledged, and the supplement provides useful implementation details and candid examples of failures involving similar sounding instances.
weaknesses: FSLA has a material specification and reproducibility problem. Algorithm 1 increments the silent-frame success counter without checking predictions, does not enforce the stated category and object-count conditions, and initializes counters outside the threshold loop. Its aggregation also does not implement the stated class averaging. Consequently, the pseudocode cannot explain the reported scores as written. This does not establish that the experimental implementation is wrong, but it prevents verification of a claimed contribution. Separately, the assertion that mAP does not penalize non-sounding predictions is too broad: false positives can reduce precision depending on their ranking.

The large-model conclusions exceed what the adaptations establish. Supplementary Sections 11.1–11.4 explicitly merge same-category masks into one identity for some methods or treat each category as one instance; Sam4AVS also retains only the top audio class. These choices structurally restrict performance on the defining instance-discrimination requirement. Table 3 demonstrates limitations of the evaluated pipelines, but does not isolate the underlying models' instance-level or temporal reasoning capabilities.

Dataset quality is supported mainly by the stated review process. The manuscript provides no quantitative annotation audit or agreement assessment and little guidance on adjudicating ambiguous sound attribution among same-category objects. The random split is described without source-grouping or near-duplicate controls. These omissions leave uncertainty about annotation reliability and independence of evaluation examples, although they do not demonstrate erroneous labels or leakage.

The methodological novelty is modest because object-token association and shifted-window processing largely follow VITA. Table 5 supports a memory-capacity tradeoff, but does not establish performance over increasing video durations or comparative end-to-end efficiency. Evaluation at 1 FPS also limits conclusions about precise sound onset and offset localization. A quantitative breakdown for simultaneous same-category sources is absent despite this being a central motivation and an acknowledged failure mode.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the useful training settings in Section 10. Training clip length and temporal sampling, fusion-module depth, and the procedure for obtaining persistent instance identities from the AVSS baselines are insufficiently specified. The supplied manuscript also provides no dataset or implementation access location. These reservations limit immediate reuse, while the benchmark contribution and established-metric gains still make the overall case favor acceptance.
